newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus investigates AIDS complaint from Briton.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus investigates AIDS complaint from Briton.

text.p: Legal loopholes and medical ethics have complicated the work of Cyprus police investigating charges a local fisherman knowingly infected a British woman with the AIDS virus, senior police sources said on Friday.
"This matter is being looked at by the Justice Ministry but there are legal difficulties. The hands of police are tied," said one police source requesting anonymity.
The 44-year-old British woman has filed a complaint with Cyprus police that the Greek Cypriot fisherman knowingly gave her AIDS, Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.
The complaint was filed last month but police have not yet questioned the man, who lives in the southeastern tourist resort of Ayia Napa.

"It is difficult to prove he has AIDS, that it was transmitted with intent and prove she got it from him. We have limited resources to investigate such behaviour, criminal though it may be" the source said, citing medical ethics.
The woman was tested HIV positive in Cyprus earlier this year and subsequently returned to England, where she is now recieving treatment.

Her complaint, filed to police last month through British lawyers, accused the Greek Cypriot of knowingly and willingly putting her at risk by having sexual intercourse with her while knowing he was HIV positive.
"He should be charged and arrested according to Cypriot law," the woman said in her complaint to Cyprus police.
Cyprus law states that a person spreading infectious diseases knowingly or through negligence is guilty of a misdemeanour, punishable by a maximum two years in prison.
